parts.title: De Isaía Prophéta

verses.text: In die illa cantábitur cánticum istud in terra Juda: Urbs fortitúdinis nostræ Sion Salvátor, ponétur in ea murus et antemurále.
Aperíte portas et ingrediátur gens justa, custódiens veritátem.
Vetus error ábiit: servábis pacem: pacem, quia in te sperávimus.
Sperástis in Dómino in sǽculis ætérnis, in Dómino Deo forti, in perpétuum.

paragraphs: Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

responsory.text: Jerúsalem, cito véniet salus tua: Quare mœróre consúmeris? numquid consiliárius non est tibi, quia innovávit te dolor?
responsory.repeat: Salvábo te, et liberábo te, noli timére.

responsory.text: Ego enim sum Dóminus, Deus tuus, Sanctus Israël, Redémptor tuus.
Salvábo te, et liberábo te, noli timére.

parts.title: Lesson from the book of Isaias

verses.text: In that day shall this canticle be sung in the land of Juda. Sion the city of our strength a saviour, a wall and a bulwark shall be set therein.
Open ye the gates, and let the just nation, that keepeth the truth, enter in.
The old error is passed away: thou wilt keep peace: peace, because we have hoped in thee.
You have hoped in the Lord for evermore, in the Lord God mighty for ever.

paragraphs: Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

responsory.text: Thy salvation cometh quickly, O Jerusalem; why art thou wasted with sorrow? Is there no counselor in thee, that pangs have taken thee?
responsory.repeat: Fear not, for I will save thee and deliver thee.

responsory.text: For I am the Lord, thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour.
Fear not, for I will save thee, and deliver thee.

verses.text: Quia incurvábit habitántes in excélso, civitátem sublímem humiliábit. Humiliábit eam usque ad terram, détrahet eam usque ad púlverem.
Sémita justi recta est, rectus callis justi ad ambulándum.
Et in sémita judiciórum tuórum, Dómine, sustinúimus te: nomen tuum, et memoriále tuum in desidério ánimæ.

paragraphs: Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

responsory.text: Ecce Dóminus véniet, et omnes Sancti ejus cum eo, et erit in die illa lux magna: et exíbunt de Jerúsalem sicut aqua munda: et regnábit Dóminus in ætérnum
Ecce Dóminus cum virtúte véniet: et regnum in manu ejus, et potéstas, et impérium.
Super omnes gentes.

verses.text: For he shall bring down them that dwell on high, the high city he shall lay low. He shall bring it down even to the ground, he shall pull it down even to the dust.
The way of the just is right, the path of the just is right to walk in.
And in the way of thy judgments, O Lord, we have patiently waited for thee: thy name, and thy remembrance are the desire of the soul.

paragraphs: Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

responsory.text: Behold, the Lord shall come, and all His saints with Him, and it shall come to pass in that day that the light shall be great; and they shall go out from Jerusalem like clean water; and the Lord shall be King for ever,
Behold, the Lord cometh with an host, and in His hand are the kingdom, and power, and dominion.
Over all the earth.

verses.text: Anima mea desiderávit te in nocte, sed et spíritu meo in præcórdiis meis de mane vigilábo ad te. Cum féceris judícia tua in terra, justítiam discent habitatóres orbis.
Misereámur ímpio, et non discet justítiam: in terra sanctórum iníqua gessit, et non vidébit glóriam Dómini.

paragraphs: Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

responsory.text: Cívitas Jerúsalem, noli flere: quóniam dóluit Dóminus super te:
responsory.repeat: Et áuferet a te omnem tribulatiónem.

responsory.text: Ecce Dóminus in fortitúdine véniet: et brácchium ejus dominábitur.
Et áuferet a te omnem tribulatiónem.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Et áuferet a te omnem tribulatiónem.

verses.text: My soul hath desired thee in the night: yea, and with my spirit within me in the morning early I will watch to thee. When thou shalt do thy judgments on the earth, the inhabitants of the world shall learn justice.
Let us have pity on the wicked, but he will not learn justice: in the land of the saints he hath done wicked things, and he shall not see the glory of the Lord.

paragraphs: Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

responsory.text: O, thou city of Jerusalem, weep not, for the Lord hath repented Him concerning thee.
responsory.repeat: And He will take away from thee all distress.

responsory.text: Behold, the Lord shall come with might, and His arm shall rule.
And He will take away from thee all distress.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
And He will take away from thee all distress.

email.html:
Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

Matins · Thursday, 10 December 2026

Thursday of the Second Week of Advent

Feria V infra Hebdomadam II Adventus · Feria major

Read in Latin and English{{listen}}

Lesson I

Lesson from the book of Isaias

Isa 26:1-4

In that day shall this canticle be sung in the land of Juda. Sion the city of our strength a saviour, a wall and a bulwark shall be set therein. Open ye the gates, and let the just nation, that keepeth the truth, enter in. The old error is passed away: thou wilt keep peace: peace, because we have hoped in thee. You have hoped in the Lord for evermore, in the Lord God mighty for ever.

Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

$Deo gratias

℟. Thy salvation cometh quickly, O Jerusalem; why art thou wasted with sorrow? Is there no counselor in thee, that pangs have taken thee? * Fear not, for I will save thee and deliver thee.

℣. For I am the Lord, thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour.

℟. Fear not, for I will save thee, and deliver thee.

Lesson II

Isa 26:5-8

For he shall bring down them that dwell on high, the high city he shall lay low. He shall bring it down even to the ground, he shall pull it down even to the dust. The way of the just is right, the path of the just is right to walk in. And in the way of thy judgments, O Lord, we have patiently waited for thee: thy name, and thy remembrance are the desire of the soul.

Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

$Deo gratias

℟. Behold, the Lord shall come, and all His saints with Him, and it shall come to pass in that day that the light shall be great; and they shall go out from Jerusalem like clean water; and the Lord shall be King for ever, * Over all the earth.

℣. Behold, the Lord cometh with an host, and in His hand are the kingdom, and power, and dominion.

℟. Over all the earth.

Lesson III

Isa 26:9-10

My soul hath desired thee in the night: yea, and with my spirit within me in the morning early I will watch to thee. When thou shalt do thy judgments on the earth, the inhabitants of the world shall learn justice. Let us have pity on the wicked, but he will not learn justice: in the land of the saints he hath done wicked things, and he shall not see the glory of the Lord.

Hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.

$Deo gratias

℟. O, thou city of Jerusalem, weep not, for the Lord hath repented Him concerning thee. * And He will take away from thee all distress.

℣. Behold, the Lord shall come with might, and His arm shall rule.

℟. And He will take away from thee all distress.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. And He will take away from thee all distress.

Read in Latin and English
